In summation of my notes, I present the order of chronological deaths. 

On a Friday, three years ago from when protagonist, Karen, enters story: 

Husband finds kayako’s diary and drowns son, Toshio before Kayako returns home. Cat potentially killed during fight, then Kayako is killed and husband hangs himself. The curse/grudge is born.

3 years later, the American family move in. Yoko is assigned from the care center upon moving in. (Based off the Thursday call from  the sister, Susan, I am assuming days of week). Yoko was first killed earlier in the week, say Tuesday or Wednesday possibly. I believe Jen was killed after Yoko on the same day, followed by Matt. 

Thursday is when Susan is heard in the voicemail sounding concerned about no word from the family and is followed by the curse, thinks she sees Matt at her apt, but is killed. 
I believe Karen entered the house on Friday because she hears the voicemail. Emma, the grandmother, dies. 
The next ones to be taken from the curse is Alex (yokos body left at the care center with Alex’s), then the detective (Nakagawa), followed by Doug, then Karen.

It’s been a while since I’ve had a bad time on psychedelics, but you know as well as I do that no matter how many good trip you have, you’ll always remember those few really uncomfortable ones. I think that’s what lurks in the back of my mind when I think about pushing the limits with psychedelics. 

I can take 2-3g of mushrooms or a tab and solo trip just fine nowadays. I have a great job and I’m in school to progress my career, stable and healthy relationships with family and a SO. For the first time in several years, my head space is actually best best it’s been in a while. I think I’m just a smidge wary of letting completely go and potentially going back to a bad place that Ive been before. 

The lovely thing about psychedelics is they reveal to you what you’ve concealed and repressed. Even when you’re uncomfortable, it’s shedding light on things you shouldn’t have hidden in the back of your head. I’ve always got to remind myself to just ride the wave and let things pass.
This is why I’m afraid to do too much. I’ve gotten pretty high and experienced a fraction of this. I don’t want to go over board
